## Annotations  schema/src/builders.ts
used by: schema-effect
/** Annotations every builder accepts: they describe the schema and never change what it accepts. */
export interface Annotations<T = unknown> {
	readonly title?: string;
	readonly description?: string;
	readonly examples?: readonly T[];
	readonly deprecated?: boolean;
	/** A default value, an annotation for tools and forms; validation never inserts it. */
	readonly default?: T;
}

used by: schema-effect
/** An array of `items`, with optional length bounds and unique items. */
export function arr<T>(
	items: Schema<T>,
	options: Annotations<T[]> & {
		readonly minItems?: number;
		readonly maxItems?: number;
		readonly uniqueItems?: boolean;
	} = {},
): Schema<T[]>

 * A bigint within optional bounds (`{ type: "bigint" }`, as TypeBox's `Type.BigInt`): an extension of JSON Schema for

## obj  schema/src/builders.ts
used by: schema-effect
/**
 * A closed object: the given properties (required unless opt()) and no others. `open: true` allows other
 * properties, as tool schemas from other systems often do.
 */
export function obj<const P extends Properties>(
	properties: P,
	options: Annotations<StaticObject<P>> & { readonly open?: boolean } = {},
): Schema<StaticObject<P>>

## opt  schema/src/builders.ts

/** Marks an obj() property as optional. */

## Optional  schema/src/builders.ts
used by: chord-effect, schema-effect
/** An optional property of obj(): `{ name: opt(str()) }` may omit `name` or set it to undefined. */
export class Optional<S extends Schema = Schema> {
	declare readonly [OPTIONAL_TYPE]?: S
	readonly schema: S
	constructor(schema: S)
}

## Properties  schema/src/builders.ts
used by: schema-effect; chord-effect via obj
/** The properties of obj(): a schema or an opt() schema per name. */
export type Properties = { readonly [name: string]: Schema | Optional };

## recursive  schema/src/builders.ts
used by: schema-effect
/**
 * A schema that contains itself, as a tree's children are trees: `build` receives a reference to the schema it
 * returns. TypeScript cannot infer a recursive type from the builders, so `T` is given:
 * `recursive<Tree>("Tree", (tree) => obj({ name: str(), children: arr(tree) }))`. `id` becomes the schema's `$id`
 * and the target of the reference, so it must be unique among the recursive schemas within one schema.
 *
 * The counterpart of TypeBox's `Type.Cyclic` + `Type.Ref`, with other JSON: an `$id` on the schema instead of `$defs`
 * and a root `$ref`. It validates the same values. The JSON differs only where a schema is published, and its type is
 * written once instead of inferred, which a recursive schema (a file tree) needs only once.
 */
export function recursive<T>(id: string, build: (self: Schema<T>) => Schema<T>): Schema<T>

## Schema  schema/src/builders.ts
used by: chord-effect, schema-effect; agent-effect via RunToolCallOptions, ai-effect via StringEnum, durable-effect via AssistantMessage, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, evals-effect via PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions
/** A JSON Schema object whose valid values have type `T` (a type-level brand; nothing extra exists at run time). */
export type Schema<T = unknown> = { readonly [keyword: string]: unknown } & { readonly [STATIC]?: T };

## Simplify  schema/src/builders.ts
used by: chord-effect via obj, schema-effect via StaticObject
type Simplify<T> = { [K in keyof T]: T[K] } & {};

## Static  schema/src/builders.ts
used by: chord-effect, schema-effect; agent-effect via AgentToolParams, ai-effect via AnthropicAllowedFallbackModel, durable-effect via SignalDefinition, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, evals-effect via PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions
// TypeBox is tested first and in its own branch: a builder brand's fallback through TypeBoxStatic would leave
// `Static<S>` of a generic `S` (constrained to builder schemas) unresolvable to its constraint's types.
/**
 * The type of the values `S` accepts: the type a builder recorded; for a TypeBox schema (`'~kind'` or `'~unsafe'`),
 * TypeBox's static type for the common kinds (see `TypeBoxStatic`); else `unknown`.
 */
export type Static<S> = S extends { readonly "~kind": unknown } | { readonly "~unsafe": unknown }
	? TypeBoxStatic<S>
	: S extends { readonly [STATIC]?: infer T }
		? unknown extends T
			? unknown
			: T
		: unknown;

## StaticObject  schema/src/builders.ts
used by: schema-effect; chord-effect via obj
/** The value type of an obj() schema. */
export type StaticObject<P extends Properties> = Simplify<
	{ -readonly [K in keyof P as P[K] extends Optional ? never : K]: Static<P[K]> } & {
		-readonly [K in keyof P as P[K] extends Optional ? K : never]?: P[K] extends Optional<infer S>
			? Static<S>
			: never;
	}
>;

## union  schema/src/builders.ts
used by: schema-effect
/**
 * Any of the given schemas. A union of objects tagged by a `lit()` property (`{ kind: lit("text"), ... }`) is checked
 * by the tag: only the branch it selects runs, and its errors are the ones reported.
 */
export function union<const S extends readonly Schema[]>(
	schemas: S,
	options: Annotations<Static<S[number]>> = {},
): Schema<Static<S[number]>>

## unsafe  schema/src/builders.ts
used by: schema-effect
/**
 * `schema` typed as accepting `T`, for values the builders cannot express (a type checked elsewhere, a schema from
 * another system). The schema is returned as it is: nothing checks that its values are `T`.
 */
export function unsafe<T>(schema: Schema = {}): Schema<T>

## deepEqual  schema/src/checks.ts
used by: schema-effect
/**
 * JSON equality, as `const`, `enum` and `uniqueItems` compare: the same primitives, arrays with equal items in order,
 * objects with the same keys and equal values (key order does not matter).
 */
export function deepEqual(a: unknown, b: unknown): boolean

## pointer  schema/src/explain.ts  watched
used by: schema-effect/src/codec.ts
why: P004: the codec writes an issue's path as the same JSON Pointer pi-schema reports (~ as ~0, / as ~1).
function pointer(path: string, key: string | number): string {
	return `${path}/${String(key).replace(/~/g, "~0").replace(/\//g, "~1")}`;
}

## KindStatic  schema/src/typebox-static.ts
used by: agent-effect via AgentToolParams, ai-effect via AnthropicAllowedFallbackModel, chord-effect via Static, durable-effect via SignalDefinition, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, evals-effect via PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions, schema-effect via Static
type KindStatic<S, K> = K extends keyof Primitives
	? Primitives[K]
	: K extends "Literal"
		? S extends { readonly const: infer V }
			? V
			: unknown
		: K extends "Array"
			? S extends { readonly items: infer I }
				? Static<I>[]
				: unknown
			: K extends "Object"
				? S extends { readonly properties: infer P }
					? ObjectStatic<P>
					: unknown
				: K extends "Union"
					? S extends { readonly anyOf: readonly (infer B)[] }
						? Static<B>
						: unknown
					: K extends "Record"
						? S extends { readonly patternProperties: infer P }
							? Record<RecordKey<keyof P>, Static<P[keyof P]>>
							: unknown
						: K extends "Enum"
							? S extends { readonly enum: readonly (infer V)[] }
								? V
								: unknown
							: K extends "Tuple"
								? S extends { readonly items: infer I extends readonly unknown[] }
									? { -readonly [N in keyof I]: Static<I[N]> }
									: unknown
								: unknown;

## ObjectStatic  schema/src/typebox-static.ts
used by: agent-effect via AgentToolParams, ai-effect via AnthropicAllowedFallbackModel, chord-effect via Static, durable-effect via SignalDefinition, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, evals-effect via PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions, schema-effect via Static
type ObjectStatic<P> = keyof P extends never
	? object
	: Simplify<
			{ -readonly [K in keyof P as P[K] extends Optional | Readonly ? never : K]: Static<P[K]> } & {
				-readonly [K in keyof P as P[K] extends Optional ? (P[K] extends Readonly ? never : K) : never]?: Static<
					P[K]
				>;
			} & {
				readonly [K in keyof P as P[K] extends Readonly ? (P[K] extends Optional ? never : K) : never]: Static<
					P[K]
				>;
			} & {
				readonly [K in keyof P as P[K] extends Optional ? (P[K] extends Readonly ? K : never) : never]?: Static<
					P[K]
				>;
			}
		>;

## RecordKey  schema/src/typebox-static.ts
used by: agent-effect via AgentToolParams, ai-effect via AnthropicAllowedFallbackModel, chord-effect via Static, durable-effect via SignalDefinition, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, evals-effect via PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions, schema-effect via Static
type RecordKey<Pattern> = Pattern extends "^-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)$" | "^-?(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)(?:\\.[0-9]+)?$"
	? number
	: string;

## Simplify  schema/src/typebox-static.ts
used by: agent-effect via AgentToolParams, ai-effect via AnthropicAllowedFallbackModel, chord-effect via Static, durable-effect via SignalDefinition, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, evals-effect via PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions, schema-effect via Static

## TypeBoxStatic  schema/src/typebox-static.ts
used by: agent-effect via AgentToolParams, ai-effect via AnthropicAllowedFallbackModel, chord-effect via Static, durable-effect via SignalDefinition, durable-rivet-effect via SqliteStorage, evals-effect via PiCodingAgentHarnessOptions, schema-effect via Static
/** The value type of a TypeBox schema type by its `'~kind'`, or its `Type.Unsafe` type; `unknown` for other kinds. */
export type TypeBoxStatic<S> = S extends { readonly "~kind": infer K }
	? KindStatic<S, K>
	: S extends { readonly "~unsafe": infer T }
		? T
		: unknown;

## Check  schema/src/types.ts
used by: schema-effect
/** A compiled boolean check. */
export type Check = (value: unknown) => boolean;

## CompileOptions  schema/src/types.ts
used by: schema-effect
/** Options of compile(). */
export interface CompileOptions {
	/** The draft whose semantics apply: "2020-12" (default) or "7". */
	readonly draft?: "2020-12" | "7";
	/**
	 * Format name to check. Without it `format` is an annotation, as draft 2020-12 specifies. The standard formats are
	 * in `@earendil-works/pi-schema/formats`.
	 */
	readonly formats?: Readonly<Record<string, FormatCheck>>;
	/** Schema documents by URI, for `$ref`s to other documents. */
	readonly schemas?: Readonly<Record<string, JsonSchema>>;
	/** Add `coerce()` and `parse()` to the validator, for loosely typed input (see the README's Coercion section). */
	readonly coerce?: boolean;
	/**
	 * What a `$ref` that names nothing (a missing definition, a document not in `schemas`) does: `"throw"` (default)
	 * makes compile() throw; `"reject"` compiles it as `false`, so only values at that place fail, with the error
	 * "unresolved reference".
	 */
	readonly unresolvedRefs?: "throw" | "reject";
}

## FormatCheck  schema/src/types.ts
used by: schema-effect
/** A format check: whether `value` (a string) has the format. */
export type FormatCheck = (value: string) => boolean;

## JsonSchema  schema/src/types.ts
used by: schema-effect; chord-effect via JobDefinition
// Public types: the schema accepted by compile(), its options, and the errors a failed value produces.

/**
 * A JSON Schema: `true`, `false` or a schema object. Schemas come from tool definitions, MCP servers and other
 * untrusted sources, so compile() reads every keyword defensively instead of trusting a static shape.
 */
export type JsonSchema = boolean | object;

## ParseResult  schema/src/types.ts
used by: schema-effect
/** The result of `parse()`: the coerced value when it is valid, else the errors of the coerced value. */
export type ParseResult<T> =
	| { readonly ok: true; readonly value: T }
	| { readonly ok: false; readonly errors: ValidationError[] };

## ValidationError  schema/src/types.ts
used by: schema-effect
/** One failure of a value: where it is (a JSON Pointer, "" for the value itself), the failing keyword and a message. */
export interface ValidationError {
	readonly path: string;
	readonly keyword: string;
	readonly message: string;
}

## CoercingValidator  schema/src/validator.ts
used by: schema-effect
/** A validator compiled with `coerce: true`: it also coerces loosely typed input towards the schema. */
export class CoercingValidator<T = unknown> extends Validator<T> {
	/**
	 * `value` coerced towards the schema: numeric strings to numbers, `"true"` to `true`, a single value to a one-item
	 * array, an optional `null` dropped, the first union branch the value converts to (the README lists every rule).
	 * Only the changed paths are copied; `value` comes back itself when nothing changes, and is never modified. Values
	 * that cannot be coerced stay as they are. The rules are built on the first call.
	 */
	coerce(value: unknown): unknown
	/** Coerces `value`, then checks it: the coerced value when it is valid, else its errors. */
	parse(value: unknown): ParseResult<T>
}

## compile  schema/src/validator.ts
used by: schema-effect
/**
 * Compiles `schema` into a Validator. Throws if the schema is malformed or a `$ref` names nothing (register other
 * documents with `options.schemas`). The schema is read, never modified. With `coerce: true` the validator also
 * coerces and parses loosely typed input.
 */
export function compile<S extends JsonSchema>(
	schema: S,
	options: CompileOptions & { readonly coerce: true },
): CoercingValidator<Static<S>>;
export function compile<S extends JsonSchema>(schema: S, options?: CompileOptions): Validator<Static<S>>;
export function compile<S extends JsonSchema>(
	schema: S,
	options: CompileOptions = NO_OPTIONS,
): Validator<Static<S>> | CoercingValidator<Static<S>>

## Validator  schema/src/validator.ts
used by: schema-effect
/** A compiled schema whose valid values have type `T` (`unknown` unless the schema was built with the builders). */
export class Validator<T = unknown> {
	/** Whether `value` is valid. A plain function: it may be passed around without its validator. */
	readonly check: (value: unknown) => value is T
	constructor(schema: JsonSchema, options: CompileOptions, check: Check)
	/**
	 * Why `value` is invalid: one error per failing keyword, `[]` when it is valid. Built on the first failure and
	 * kept, so a validator whose values always pass never pays for it.
	 */
	errors(value: unknown): ValidationError[]
	/**
	 * `value` itself when it is valid, else its errors: check() and errors() in one result, without coercion.
	 *
	 * Not TypeBox's `Value.Parse`, which also clones, fills defaults, converts and strips undeclared properties before
	 * it checks. This only checks: the strict replacement where `Value.Parse` is used to validate (its other steps
	 * change nothing for a valid value of a schema without defaults or extra properties). Use `parse()` with
	 * `coerce: true` for conversion.
	 */
	validate(value: unknown): ParseResult<T>
}
